 In 2025, After $50 Million Defamation Verdict, Jack Nicklaus Buys Back His Namesake Company
 Miracle Dimwesh 2026년 11월 15일 일 오후 3:22 UTC 0 A courtroom victory and a carefully structured acquisition have brought Jack Nicklaus back together with the business built around his name.
 The golf legend completed the purchase of Nicklaus Companies in March 2026 through 20 Majors, LLC, involving Nicklaus, TWG Global and Nicklaus Brown . A bankruptcy court approved the $35.7 million deal, restoring his name, image and likeness rights, plus trademarks and licensing rights, including the Golden Bear.
 The transaction followed a $50 million defamation verdict against Nicklaus Companies in October 2025. A Florida jury found the company had spread false claims that Nicklaus negotiated a $750 million agreement to become LIV Golf’s public face.
 Nicklaus said he met Saudi golf representatives to discuss designing a course but rejected an approach involving LIV. The jury sided with him, while clearing former owner Howard Milstein and executive Andrew O’Brien of individual liability.
 The dispute began with an earlier business arrangement. Nicklaus sold rights to his course design, club brand and Golden Bear clothing business in 2007 for $145 million. He left daily operations in 2017 and the company’s board in 2022.
 Jack Nicklaus Aaron Doster-Imagn Images The legal fight intensified after Nicklaus resumed course-design work following the expiration of a five-year non-compete agreement. The company sued, prompting his defamation countersuit in 2023.
 The acquisition puts his design projects and brand assets under the same ownership. Nicklaus Design has projects worldwide, while the Golden Bear remains one of golf’s most recognizable marks.
 TWG Global, led by Los Angeles Dodgers and Lakers owner Mark Walter, joined Nicklaus in the investment group. The deal gives the 86-year-old a chance to rebuild the business after years of legal conflict.
 For Nicklaus, the outcome goes beyond damages. He has regained the commercial identity that helped define his career, closing a costly chapter after years of legal conflict and securing it for future generations.
